title.value: One Self, Many Strikes: Geophone Evidence for a Distributed Self at the Basin Rim of The Sump, With a Note on the Convergence at the Ring

abstract.value: Percussive activity around the basin rim has been described since the first survey as an exchange between separated drumming groups. Six years of geophone coverage show instead a single response pattern propagating around the rim with no evidence of turn-taking, no addressee structure, and a latency profile consistent with one body distributed across eighty kilometres of floor. The convergence at the ring, previously read as a meeting, appears on this evidence to be closer to a change of posture. We are conscious that we are describing something whose boundary we cannot find, and we do not claim to have found it here.
